paper.title: OSOM: A simultaneously optimal algorithm for multi-armed and linear contextual bandits

settings.name_in_paper: Simple Model (multi-armed bandit, rewards independent of contexts)
unmapped: Mean rewards mu_i in [-1,1], independent of the observed contexts (theta*=0 case of the complex model); learner does not know which model holds
Contexts still observed and satisfy the stochastic assumption (zero conditional mean, covariance >= rho_min I, unit-norm, independent across arms)
The learner knows the context eigenvalue parameters rho_min and rho_max (used in the test threshold)
settings.definition_quote: Under the simple multi-armed bandit model, the mean rewards of K arms are fixed and are not a function of the contexts. That is, at each round g_{i,t} = \mu_i + \eta_{i,t} where \mu_i \in [-1,1], {\eta_{i,t}} are identical, independent, zero mean, \sigma-sub-Gaussian noise.

settings.name_in_paper: Complex Model (linear contextual bandit with arm biases)
unmapped: Reward g_{i,t} = mu_i + <theta*, alpha_{i,t}> + eta_{i,t}: shared theta* plus unknown per-arm biases mu_i in [-1,1]
Contexts alpha_{i,t} in unit ball drawn independently of the past, independent across arms, zero conditional mean, conditional covariance Sigma_c >= rho_min I
The learner knows the context eigenvalue parameters rho_min and rho_max
Per-round contexts (K vectors in R^d) are drawn stochastically, so the action set changes each round
settings.definition_quote: In this complex model, we assume there exists an underlying linear predictor \theta^* \in R^d and biases [\mu_1,...,\mu_K] of the K arms, such that the mean rewards of the arms are affine functions of the contexts, that is, g_{i,t} = \mu_i + <\theta^*, \alpha_{i,t}> + \eta_{i,t}. We impose boundedness constraints on the parameters: in particular, we have \mu_i \in [-1,1], \theta^* \in B_2^d(1).

conditions: contexts satisfy the stochastic assumption: unit norm, zero conditional mean, conditional covariance >= rho_min I, independent across arms

source.label: thm:mainregretbound
source.quote: With probability at least $1 - 33\delta$, we obtain the following upper bounds on regret for the algorithm OSOM: (a) Under the Simple Model $R^s_n \le \sigma\cdot \sum_{i:\Delta_i >0} \left[3\Delta_i + \frac{16}{\Delta_i}\log\left(\frac{2Kn}{\Delta_i \delta}\right)\right]$.

results.notes: Regret R^s_n = n mu* - sum mu_{A_s} (pseudo-regret through means) but bound holds with high probability. sigma multiplies the whole bracket as printed (proof via Abbasi-Yadkori Thm 7 gives it without sigma). Theorem states 1-33delta; proof of part (a) gives 1-18delta.

symbols.rho_min: lower bound on the minimum eigenvalue of the context covariance Sigma_c
symbols.rho_max: conditional sub-Gaussian parameter of the context vectors (<= 1)

conditions: contexts alpha_{i,t} in unit ball, drawn independent of the past, independent across arms, zero conditional mean, conditional covariance Sigma_c >= rho_min I > 0

source.label: thm:mainregretbound
source.quote: With probability at least $1 - 33\delta$ ... (b) Under the Complex Model $\regret{n} \le 4(K+1) + 4 \mathcal{W}_{\delta/n}(n,n) = \widetilde{\mathcal{O}}\left\{\sigma\left(\sqrt{\frac{ \higheig}{\loweig}} \cdot \sqrt{d}+\sqrt{K}\right)\sqrt{n}\right\}$.

results.notes: Regret against per-round best arm under linear model, defined through means; holds w.h.p. The exact form 4(K+1)+4W_{delta/n}(n,n) uses a complex function W defined in the paper; only the O_tilde form recorded.
